en: selection (for a role or position); being picked out

examples.ko: 신인 배우의 주연 발탁이 화제가 됐어요.
examples.en: The casting of a newcomer in the lead role became a hot topic.

examples.ko: 그 선수는 국가대표 발탁을 꿈꿔 왔어요.
examples.en: That player has dreamed of being picked for the national team.
Everyone was surprised by the sudden selection.

examples.ko: 젊은 직원의 부장 발탁은 회사에서 처음이에요.
examples.en: A young employee being picked for department head is a first for the company.

examples.ko: 감독의 발탁 기준은 실력이 아니라 성실함이었어요.
examples.en: The coach's selection criterion was diligence, not skill.
I teared up when I heard the news that I was chosen.

explain: '발탁'은 많은 사람 중에서 쓸 만한 사람을 골라 특별한 자리에 올려 쓰는 일에 써요. 그냥 '선택'과 달리 고르는 쪽이 윗사람이고, 뽑힌 사람이 좋은 기회를 얻는다는 느낌이 있어요. '신인 발탁', '파격 발탁'처럼 써요.

phrases.en: The coach's bold pick is the talk of the town.
phrases.nuance_ko: 예상 밖의 사람을 뽑았을 때 쓰는 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common pairing for an unexpected, bold selection.

phrases.en: That player was selected for the national team.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뽑히는 사람 입장에서 말하는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The expression from the point of view of the person who is picked.

phrases.en: Everyone was surprised by this selection of personnel.
phrases.nuance_ko: 회사나 정부에서 사람을 골라 새 자리에 앉히는 일을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for choosing people for new posts in a company or government.

explain_en: 발탁 is for choosing a promising person out of many and putting them in a special position. Unlike plain 선택, the chooser is in a higher position and the person picked gets a good opportunity. Typical uses are 신인 발탁 and 파격 발탁.

examples.ko: 회사는 신입 사원을 교육 성적에 따라 부서에 배속해요.
examples.en: The company places new employees in departments based on their training scores.

examples.ko: 인사팀에서 저를 이번 달부터 마케팅팀에 배속했어요.
examples.en: HR assigned me to the marketing team starting this month.

examples.ko: 신입을 어느 부서에 배속할지 아직 정하지 못했어요.
examples.en: We haven't decided yet which department to place the new hire in.

examples.ko: 신병을 각 부대에 배속하는 일은 며칠 걸려요.
examples.en: Assigning new recruits to each unit takes a few days.

examples.ko: 희망한 부서에 배속해 주셔서 정말 감사해요.
examples.en: Thank you so much for placing me in the department I wanted.

examples.ko: 새로 온 간호사들을 응급실에 배속하기로 했대요.
examples.en: I heard they decided to place the new nurses in the emergency room.

explain: '배치하다'는 사람이나 물건을 자리에 두는 일 전반에 쓰고, '배속하다'는 사람을 부서나 부대에 소속시킬 때 써요. '~에 배속하다'처럼 조사 '에'와 함께 쓰고, 말할 때는 '발령 나다'도 많이 써요.

phrases.en: I was assigned to the sales team starting this month.
phrases.nuance_ko: '배속하다'의 피동형으로, 배치를 받는 사람 입장에서 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The passive form of '배속하다', said from the viewpoint of the person being assigned.

phrases.example: 회사는 신입 사원을 고객팀에 배속하기로 했어요.
phrases.en: The company decided to assign the new employees to the customer team.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부서를 정했다고 말할 때 쓰는 연결형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A connected form used when saying a department has been decided.

phrases.example: 다음 달에 부산 지점으로 발령 나요.
phrases.en: I will be posted to the Busan branch next month.
phrases.nuance_ko: '배속하다'보다 말할 때 더 자주 쓰는 쉬운 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easier expression used more often in speech than '배속하다'.

explain_en: '배치하다' covers putting people or things in a spot in general, while '배속하다' is for attaching a person to a department or unit. It takes the particle '에' as in '~에 배속하다', and in speech people also say '발령 나다'.

examples.en: The hospital director met the patient in person.
I greeted the hospital director.
The newly arrived director has a reputation for being kind.
To see the hospital director, you must make an appointment.
The hospital director and the doctors held a meeting together.
Everyone listened quietly to the director's words.

explain: '-장'은 어떤 곳의 책임자 이름에 붙어요. 학교는 '교장', 병원은 '병원장', 회사는 '사장'처럼 곳마다 말이 달라요. 높여 부를 때는 '님'을 붙여 '병원장님'이라고 해요.

phrases.en: The hospital director said so.
phrases.nuance_ko: 높여 부르거나 말할 때 '님'을 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add '님' to show respect.

phrases.en: The director's office is on the third floor.
phrases.nuance_ko: 병원장이 일하는 방이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The room where the hospital director works.

phrases.en: The new hospital director came to work for the first time today.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람이 바뀌었을 때 '새'를 앞에 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put '새' in front when the person has changed.

explain_en: The ending '-장' marks the head of a place, and each place has its own word: '교장' for a school, '병원장' for a hospital, '사장' for a company. To show respect add '님', as in '병원장님'.

examples.en: I assist the team leader.
The secretary assisted the president from his side.
Ten staff members assist the mayor.

examples.ko: 새 총리를 보좌하고 일을 배우고 있어요.
examples.en: I'm assisting the new prime minister and learning the job.
I came to work early to assist the mayor.
We're hiring someone to assist the CEO.

explain: 윗사람이 일을 잘하도록 곁에서 돕는다는 뜻이라서 도움을 받는 사람이 나보다 높은 자리예요. 친구를 돕는 일에는 '도와주다'를 쓰고, 이 말은 쓰지 않아요.

phrases.en: He works as an aide to the minister.
phrases.nuance_ko: 도움을 받는 윗사람을 '~을/를'로 함께 말하는 가장 기본적인 모양이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The basic pattern, naming the superior being assisted with '~을/를'.

phrases.example: 그는 오 년째 대표를 보좌하고 있어요.
phrases.en: He has been assisting the CEO for five years.
phrases.nuance_ko: 계속 이어지는 일을 말할 때 '-고 있다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: -고 있다 is used for something that is still going on.

phrases.en: The secretary helps the president from beside him.
phrases.nuance_ko: '보좌하다'를 쉬운 말로 풀어 쓴 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A simpler way to say 보좌하다.

explain_en: It means helping a superior do their job well from close by, so the person helped holds a higher position. For helping a friend, use 도와주다 instead.

en: to resign; to retire; to step down

examples.en: The manager stepped down because of poor results.
The CEO plans to resign next month.
He decided to resign and take responsibility.
On the day he resigned, he left a letter for the staff.
The university president resigned suddenly, and the school became noisy with talk.
After resigning, he went back to his hometown.

explain: '사임하다'는 높은 직책에서 스스로 물러날 때 써요. 일반 회사를 그만두는 말은 '퇴사하다'이고, '그만두다'가 가장 일상적이에요. 윗사람이 내보내는 경우는 '해임하다'라서 누가 결정했는지가 달라요.

phrases.en: He took responsibility and stepped down on his own.
phrases.nuance_ko: 남이 시키지 않았다는 점을 강조해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Stresses that nobody forced it.

phrases.en: The chairman decided to step down at the end of this year.
phrases.nuance_ko: 그만두기로 마음먹었을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when someone has decided to leave a post.

phrases.en: He stepped down as CEO because of his health.
phrases.nuance_ko: '직'과 함께 어떤 자리에서 물러나는지 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: With '직', it names the post being left.

explain_en: '사임하다' is for stepping down from a high post by choice. Leaving an ordinary company is '퇴사하다', and '그만두다' is the everyday word. If a superior removes the person it's '해임하다', so who decides differs.

examples.en: The team leader stepped down to take responsibility.

examples.ko: 감독이 성적 때문에 사퇴할 거라는 소문이 있어요.
examples.en: There's a rumor the coach will resign over the results.

examples.ko: 그 후보는 선거 전에 사퇴하기로 했어요.
examples.en: That candidate decided to withdraw before the election.
His health got worse, so he resigned as chairman.
Calls for him to resign keep coming.

examples.ko: 반장이 갑자기 사퇴해서 반 친구들이 놀랐어요.
examples.en: The class president suddenly quit, and the classmates were surprised.

explain: '그만두다'는 어디에나 쓰지만 '사퇴하다'는 회장, 감독, 위원, 후보처럼 맡은 자리나 후보 자리를 내려놓을 때 써요. 회사를 떠나는 건 '퇴사하다'가 자연스러워요.

phrases.en: The coach took responsibility and stepped down.
phrases.nuance_ko: '사퇴하다'보다 쉬워서 일상 대화에서도 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Easier than 사퇴하다 and common in everyday talk.

phrases.en: The chairman announced his resignation yesterday.
phrases.nuance_ko: 그만둔다고 공식적으로 알릴 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A phrase for officially announcing one is leaving a post.

phrases.en: The fans demand the coach's resignation.
phrases.nuance_ko: 다른 사람에게 자리에서 내려오라고 할 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A phrase for demanding that someone leave their post.

explain_en: 그만두다 works almost anywhere, but 사퇴하다 is for giving up a post or candidacy, such as chairperson, coach, committee member, or candidate. Leaving a company is more naturally 퇴사하다.

en: to be appointed; to be elected

examples.en: Department head Kim was appointed as the new team leader.
Let me introduce the person who was appointed society president.
He was unanimously chosen as the representative.

examples.ko: 새 감독이 선임되면 팀이 달라질 거예요.
examples.en: When a new coach is appointed, the team will change.
An outside expert is appointed as a committee member.
As soon as he was appointed, he started reforms.

explain: 회사나 단체에서 사람이 어떤 자리를 맡도록 정해질 때 써요. 말로는 '뽑히다', '임명되다'도 써요. '선임'은 순서가 먼저인 사람, 즉 선배라는 뜻도 있으니 문장을 잘 봐야 해요.

phrases.en: He was appointed as the new representative.
phrases.nuance_ko: 윗사람이나 기관이 그 자리를 맡기는 느낌이 강해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Stronger sense that someone in authority assigns the post.

phrases.en: I was chosen as class president.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상에서 더 쉽게 쓰는 말이고, 투표나 선택으로 골라질 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A more everyday word, used when someone is chosen by vote or selection.

phrases.en: He was appointed as the company's representative.
phrases.nuance_ko: '자리 이름 + (으)로 선임되다' 모양으로 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Typically used in the pattern 'position + 로 선임되다'.

explain_en: Used when a person is chosen for a post in a company or organization. In speech '뽑히다' or '임명되다' also work. Note that '선임' can also mean a senior person, so read the context.

en: to belong to; to be affiliated

examples.en: I belong to the marketing team.

examples.ko: 이 선수는 어느 팀에 소속되어 있어요?
examples.en: Which team is this player affiliated with?

examples.ko: 두 사람은 같은 동아리에 소속되어 있었어요.
examples.en: The two of them belonged to the same club.
My department changed, so I moved my seat.

examples.ko: 학교에 소속되지 않은 강사도 참여할 수 있어요.
examples.en: Instructors not affiliated with the school can take part too.

examples.ko: 신입 직원은 다음 달에 영업부에 소속될 거예요.
examples.en: The new employee will be assigned to the sales department next month.

explain: 회사·학교·팀처럼 어딘가의 한 구성원일 때 써요. 보통 '~에 소속되어 있다'로 말해요. 일상에서는 '~에서 일해요', '~ 팀이에요'가 더 자연스럽고, 명사 '소속'을 '소속이 어디예요?'처럼 쓰기도 해요.

phrases.en: Excuse me, where do you belong (which company or team)?
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 '소속'을 써서 어느 회사나 팀인지 물어볼 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Uses the noun 소속 to ask which company or team someone is part of.

phrases.example: 저는 아직 어느 팀에도 소속되어 있지 않아요.
phrases.en: I don't belong to any team yet.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어디에도 속하지 않은 상태를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Says someone is not a member of any group.

phrases.en: I work at this company.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서 '소속되다'보다 더 자연스러운 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: More natural in daily talk than 소속되다.

explain_en: Use it when you are a member of a company, school, team, or similar group. It is usually said as '~에 소속되어 있다'. In daily conversation, '~에서 일해요' or '~ 팀이에요' sounds more natural, and the noun '소속' is also used, as in '소속이 어디예요?'.

dis.h: be affiliated with an organization; passive form
gh: active form, rarer; belong to organization

examples.ko: 회사 수뇌부가 오늘 긴급 회의를 열었어요.
examples.en: The company's top executives held an emergency meeting today.
We are waiting for an announcement from the government leadership.

examples.ko: 수뇌부는 이번 계획을 바꾸지 않기로 했어요.
examples.en: The leadership decided not to change this plan.
The manager talked with the club's top management for a long time.

examples.ko: 수뇌부에 있는 사람들은 현장 사정을 잘 몰라요.
examples.en: The people in the top leadership don't know the situation on the ground well.

examples.ko: 그 조직의 수뇌부를 만나려면 약속이 필요해요.
examples.en: You need an appointment to meet that organization's leadership.

explain: 회사, 정부, 단체에서 가장 높은 자리에 있는 사람들을 하나의 집단으로 부르는 말이에요. 한 사람을 가리킬 때는 쓰지 않아요. 일상에서는 '임원진', '윗분들'이라고 하고, '수뇌부'는 뉴스에서 자주 나와요. 반대로 현장은 '일선'이라고 해요.

phrases.en: The company's top leadership decided on the new plan.
phrases.nuance_ko: 조직의 이름 뒤에 붙여 그 조직의 가장 높은 사람들을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Attached after an organization's name to mean its top people.

phrases.en: A leadership meeting was held this morning.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가장 높은 사람들이 모이는 회의를 말하고 뉴스에서 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: A meeting of the top people, often seen in news.

phrases.en: The executives greeted the employees.
phrases.nuance_ko: 수뇌부보다 쉽고 회사 이야기에서 일상적으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Easier than 수뇌부 and common in everyday talk about companies.

explain_en: It refers to the people in the highest positions of a company, government or group, taken as a whole, not a single person. In daily life people say '임원진' or '윗분들', while '수뇌부' appears often in the news. The opposite side is the front line, '일선'.

examples.en: Our team was promoted to the first division.

examples.ko: 이 마을은 내년에 시로 승격할 예정이에요.
examples.en: This village is going to be upgraded to a city next year.

examples.ko: 작은 연구소가 국가 기관으로 승격하면 지원이 늘어요.
examples.en: If the small institute is upgraded to a national agency, support will increase.
We waited a long time for the school to be upgraded to a university.

examples.ko: 승격한 팀의 선수들이 기쁨의 눈물을 흘렸어요.
examples.en: The players of the promoted team shed tears of joy.

examples.ko: 부서가 본부로 승격하면서 사람이 더 필요해졌어요.
examples.en: As the department was upgraded to a headquarters, more people became necessary.

explain: 사람의 직급이 오를 때는 '승진하다'를 쓰고, 승격하다는 팀·부서·마을·기관·리그처럼 조직이나 등급이 한 단계 높아질 때 써요. 'A가 B로 승격하다'처럼 '(으)로'를 붙여요. 반대말은 '강등되다'예요.

phrases.en: This school was promoted to a university this year.
phrases.nuance_ko: 스스로 하는 것이 아니라 올려졌다는 뜻이라 뉴스에서 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means it was raised by others, so it is common in the news.

phrases.en: The company promoted this team to a division.
phrases.nuance_ko: 누군가 등급을 올려 줄 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when someone raises the rank of something.

phrases.en: Promotion to the first league has been confirmed.
phrases.nuance_ko: 스포츠 소식에서 자주 보이는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A pairing often seen in sports news.

explain_en: When a person moves up in rank, use '승진하다'. '승격하다' is for an organization or level going up a step, such as a team, department, town, institution or league. The pattern is 'A가 B로 승격하다'. The opposite is '강등되다'.

examples.en: If you pass the exam, you advance to the next level next month.

examples.ko: 올해는 평가 점수가 좋아서 승급 대상에 들어갔어요.
examples.en: My evaluation score was good this year, so I made the list for advancement.
When you move up a grade, your base pay rises one step.
He advanced a rank in the taekwondo belt test.
I didn't advance, so I have to wait until next year.
My colleague moved up first, so I congratulated them.

explain: 급수, 등급, 호봉처럼 '급'이 올라갈 때 써요. 직위가 올라갈 때는 '승진하다'를 쓰고, '승급'은 월급 단계나 실력 등급이 오르는 데 더 잘 맞아요. 태권도 띠나 시험 급수 이야기에도 나와요.

phrases.en: I take the level-promotion exam next week.
phrases.nuance_ko: 다음 급수로 올라가기 위해 보는 시험을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The exam taken to move up to the next level.

phrases.en: I moved up one level in taekwondo.
phrases.nuance_ko: 급이 한 칸 올라갔다는 점을 분명히 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Makes clear that the level went up by one step.

phrases.en: I worked steadily and was moved up to the advanced class.
phrases.nuance_ko: 스스로 올라가기보다 평가를 받아 올라간 느낌을 줘요.
phrases.nuance_en: Gives the sense of being moved up by evaluation.

explain_en: Use it when a grade, level or pay step goes up. When a job position goes up, use '승진하다'; '승급' fits pay steps and skill levels better. It also appears in talk about taekwondo belts and exam levels.

examples.en: The bus driver greeted the passengers.
My father worked as a taxi driver for a long time.

examples.ko: 운전수 아저씨가 길을 잘 알고 계세요.
examples.en: The driver knows the way well.
I saw an ad looking for a truck driver.
Drivers must be careful about drowsy driving.
I heard Grandfather's house had a separate chauffeur.

explain: 직업으로 차를 모는 사람을 말하는데, '운전수'는 오래된 느낌이 있어요. 지금은 '운전기사'나 '기사님'이 더 정중해서 많이 써요. 직접 부를 때는 '기사님'이라고 해요.

phrases.en: The taxi driver knows the roads well.
phrases.nuance_ko: '운전수'보다 정중해서 지금은 더 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: More polite than 운전수 and more widely used now.

phrases.en: Driver, please stop here.
phrases.nuance_ko: 운전하는 분을 직접 부를 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: What you call the driver directly.

phrases.example: 저는 커서 버스 운전수가 되고 싶어요.
phrases.en: When I grow up, I want to become a bus driver.
phrases.nuance_ko: 직업을 말할 때 쓰지만 조금 오래된 느낌이 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for a job, but sounds a bit dated.

explain_en: It means a person who drives a vehicle as a job, but 운전수 sounds old-fashioned. Today 운전기사 or 기사님 is more polite and common. When addressing the person directly, say 기사님.

examples.en: The city appointed that professor as a committee member.

examples.ko: 회사는 다음 달에 새 자문위원을 위촉할 거예요.
examples.en: The company will appoint a new advisor next month.

examples.ko: 대표가 분야별 전문가 세 명을 직접 위촉해요.
examples.en: The head personally appoints three experts, one for each field.
The ceremony to appoint the ambassador is held today.

examples.ko: 협회에서 저를 심사위원으로 위촉해서 정말 놀랐어요.
examples.en: I was really surprised that the association appointed me as a judge.

examples.ko: 위원을 위촉하기 전에 이름을 먼저 확인해요.
examples.en: Before appointing the members, we check the names first.

explain: 공식적으로 일을 맡길 때 쓰는 말이라 친구 사이에서는 거의 안 써요. '위원으로 위촉하다'처럼 '-(으)로'와 같이 쓰고, 맡는 쪽은 '위촉되다'라고 해요. '임명하다'는 자기 조직 사람에게 직책을 주는 느낌이고, 위촉은 바깥 전문가에게 부탁해서 맡기는 느낌이에요.

phrases.en: He was appointed as a judge.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일을 맡는 쪽에서 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used from the side of the person given the role.

phrases.en: The city appointed the singer as a goodwill ambassador.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-(으)로 위촉하다'로 공식 직책을 줄 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: '-(으)로 위촉하다' is for giving an official role.

phrases.en: I received a letter of appointment yesterday.
phrases.nuance_ko: 위촉할 때 주는 공식 문서예요.
phrases.nuance_en: The official paper given when someone is commissioned.

explain_en: This is a formal word, so you will hardly hear it between friends. It is used with '-(으)로' as in '위원으로 위촉하다', and the person who receives the role is described with '위촉되다'. '임명하다' feels like giving a post to someone inside your own organization, while 위촉하다 feels like asking an outside expert to take the role.

examples.en: Only the president has authority over employee personnel decisions.
The person with personnel authority decides promotions.
There is controversy over the president's appointment powers.

examples.ko: 팀장은 인사권이 없어서 채용을 못 해요.
examples.en: A team leader has no hiring authority, so they can't recruit.

examples.ko: 인사권을 함부로 쓰면 직원들이 불만을 가져요.
examples.en: If you use personnel power carelessly, employees become dissatisfied.
The company's personnel authority belongs only to the CEO.

explain: 여기서 '인사'는 인사하다의 인사가 아니라 사람을 뽑고 배치하고 승진시키는 일이에요. 그런 권한을 가진 사람은 '인사권자'라고 해요. 회사나 정치 뉴스에서 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: The person with personnel authority decides on department transfers.
phrases.nuance_ko: 인사권을 가진 사람을 가리키는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the person who holds personnel authority.
phrases.en_equiv: the person in charge of personnel decisions

phrases.en: The CEO used his personnel authority to replace the team leader.
phrases.nuance_ko: 그 권한을 실제로 사용할 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A pairing for actually using that authority.

phrases.en: The boss handed personnel authority over to the team leader.
phrases.nuance_ko: 권한을 다른 사람에게 맡길 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when delegating that authority to someone else.

explain_en: Here '인사' is not the greeting from '인사하다'; it means hiring, assigning and promoting people. The person with that power is called '인사권자'. It appears often in business and political news.
